directAnswer: A typical WiFi router can reach up to 150 feet indoors and about 300 feet outdoors, depending on the environment and obstacles.
summary: WiFi range can vary based on several factors, including the type of router, frequency band, and physical barriers.

sections.heading: Factors Affecting WiFi Range
sections.body: The range of a WiFi router is influenced by several factors such as the frequency band (2.4 GHz has a longer range than 5 GHz), physical obstacles like walls and furniture, and the power of the router itself.

sections.heading: How to Improve WiFi Range
sections.body: To enhance the WiFi coverage, consider repositioning the router to a central location, using WiFi extenders, or upgrading to a more powerful router.

steps.title: Reposition Your Router
steps.detail: Place the router in a central location in your home, away from walls and obstructions.

steps.title: Use a WiFi Extender
steps.detail: Install a WiFi extender to boost the signal in areas with weak coverage.

steps.title: Upgrade Your Router
steps.detail: Consider upgrading to a dual-band or tri-band router for better coverage and speed.

faqs.question: Can walls affect WiFi signal strength?
faqs.answer: Yes, walls, especially those made of concrete or brick, can significantly weaken WiFi signals.

faqs.question: Does the number of connected devices impact range?
faqs.answer: Yes, more connected devices can reduce the overall bandwidth and may affect performance, but they do not directly affect the physical range.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands?
faqs.answer: The 2.4 GHz band has a longer range but lower speeds, while the 5 GHz band offers faster speeds but a shorter range.

caveats: Actual range may vary based on environmental factors, interference from other devices, and router specifications.
